slides.title: Spoken Tutorial on Your First AI Application
slides.narration: Welcome to this Spoken Tutorial on **Your First AI Application**.

slides.title: Learning Objectives
slides.narration:
In this tutorial, you will learn to,

• Explain what an **API** is.
• Identify how to get a **Google AI Studio API key**.
• Apply **Python** code to interact with the **Gemini API**.
• Generate marketing slogans using an **AI** model.

slides.title: System Requirements
slides.narration: Here I am using a browser on a computer or mobile.

slides.title: Prerequisites
slides.narration:
To follow this tutorial, you should have watched **Episode 1**.
Also watch **Episode 2** of this **Module**.

slides.title: What is an API?
slides.narration:
What exactly is an **API**?
Think of an **API**, or **Application Programming Interface**.
It is like a waiter in a restaurant.
You tell the waiter what you want.
The waiter then communicates with the kitchen to get it.
You don't need to know how the food is prepared.
Similarly, an **API** connects your application to a server.
slides.image_prompt: Illustration showing an API as a waiter connecting a customer (application) to a kitchen (server)

slides.title: Introducing the Gemini API
slides.narration:
Now, let's introduce the **Gemini API**.
Continuing our analogy, the **Gemini API** is like a specialized chef.
This chef can create unique dishes, such as marketing slogans.
It does this based on your specific requests.
It makes **Google's** powerful **AI** model accessible to developers.
slides.image_prompt: Illustration showing Gemini API as a specialized chef creating unique dishes like marketing slogans

slides.title: Step 1: Get Your API Key
slides.narration:
First, navigate to **Google AI Studio**.
**Sign in** with your **Google** account.
**Click** on **Get API key**.
This creates a new **API key**.
Then, **copy** this **API key**.
Remember to keep your **API key** secure.
slides.image_prompt: Browser showing Google AI Studio interface with 'Get API key' button highlighted, user clicking it

slides.title: Step 2: Open Google Colab
slides.narration:
Next, open a new **Google Colab** notebook.
Do this directly in your browser.
**Google Colab** provides a **Python** environment.
Here you will write and run your code.
slides.image_prompt: Browser showing a new Google Colab notebook interface

slides.title: Step 3: Install & Configure Gemini API
slides.narration:
In **Colab**, first install the generative **AI** package.
Use `!pip install` for this.
Then, **import** and configure it.
Use your copied **API key** with `genai.configure`.
slides.image_prompt: Screen close-up: user typing '!pip install google-generativeai' and 'genai.configure(api_key="YOUR_API_KEY")' in Google Colab

slides.title: Step 4: Initialize the Gemini Model
slides.narration:
Now, initialize the **gemini-pro** model.
Create an instance of `genai.GenerativeModel`.
This prepares the model.
It will then receive your **prompts**.
slides.image_prompt: Screen close-up: user typing 'model = genai.GenerativeModel("gemini-pro")' in Google Colab

slides.title: Vague Prompt Example: Defining Product
slides.narration:
Let us define our product topic.
Store it in a variable.
For example, `product_topic = 'a new brand of eco-friendly sneakers'`.
This will be the basis for our marketing slogans.
slides.image_prompt: Screen close-up: user typing 'product_topic = 'a new brand of eco-friendly sneakers'' in Google Colab

slides.title: Improved Prompt: Crafting Slogans
slides.narration:
Now, let's craft an improved **prompt**.
Make it clear and specific.
For example, `prompt = f"Create 5 catchy marketing slogans for {product_topic}"`.
This guides the **AI** model.
It generates relevant output.
slides.image_prompt: Screen close-up: user typing 'prompt = f"Create 5 catchy marketing slogans for {product_topic}"' in Google Colab

slides.title: Comparing Prompt Effectiveness
slides.narration:
Let's compare **prompt** effectiveness.
A vague **prompt**, like 'slogans for sneakers', gives generic results.
But a specific **prompt** directs the **AI**.
For example, a prompt can be crafted.
Use 'Create 5 catchy marketing slogans for a new brand of eco-friendly sneakers'.
This produces targeted and useful output.
slides.image_prompt: Side-by-side: vague prompt 'slogans for sneakers' output vs improved prompt 'Create 5 catchy marketing slogans for a new brand of eco-friendly sneakers' output

slides.title: Step 5: Run Your AI Application
slides.narration:
Now, run your **AI** application.
**Press** the **play button** next to your code block in **Colab**.
The **AI** processes your **prompt**.
It will **print** the generated marketing slogans.
This happens in a few seconds.
slides.image_prompt: Google Colab screen showing code block with play button, AI generating response below

slides.title: Challenge: Experiment with Products
slides.narration:
Here is a challenge for you.
Modify the `product_topic` variable.
Explore different products, like 'a new spicy hot sauce'.
Or try 'a productivity app'.
Observe the **AI's** varied slogan creations.
slides.image_prompt: Screen close-up: user modifying 'product_topic' variable in Google Colab, with a thought bubble indicating experimentation

slides.title: Summary
slides.narration:
Let us summarize what we learned.
We learned about **APIs**.
We obtained an **API key**.
We set up **Google Colab**.
Finally, we built our first **AI** application.
This generates marketing slogans using the **Gemini API**.

slides.title: Assignment
slides.narration:
Now, for an assignment, experiment with different product topics.
Also, try various **prompt** structures.
Generate diverse marketing slogans.
Try to add constraints to your **prompt**.
For example, add constraints like 'slogans under 10 words'.
Compare the results.
